chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Sayf, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, who said:
I said to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام): “Describe to me the Prophet of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله).”

He said: “The Prophet of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was fair, tinged with redness, intensely black-eyed, with eyebrows nearly joined, broad at the extremities, as though gold had been poured over his fingers, and with great shoulder joints.”

When he turned, he would turn completely. The line of hair on his chest flowed from the hollow of his throat to his navel, as though it were a streak in purified silver. His neck up to his shoulders was like a silver ewer. His nose would nearly reach the water when he drank. When he walked, he leaned forward as though descending a slope. None like the Prophet of Allah was ever seen before him nor after him (صلى الله عليه وآله).

key_terms.أَدْعَجَ الْعَيْنَيْنِ: having intensely dark and striking eyes
key_terms.تَكَفَّأَ: he leaned forward in his gait
key_terms.سُرْبَتُهُ: the fine line of hair running down the chest
key_terms.شَثْنَ الْأَطْرَافِ: broad or full in the extremities
key_terms.كَاهِلِهِ: the upper back or shoulder area

ai.seo_question: How does al-Kāfī describe the physical appearance of the Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله)?
ai.summary: This hadith records a physical description of the Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) as narrated from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام). It highlights his noble appearance, dignified manner of turning and walking, and the uniqueness of his form among all people before and after him.
